name: handlename
description: handlename's personal Claude Code plugins, one plugin per skill

plugins.name: handlename-commit-it
plugins.description: Commit changes following the Conventional Commits specification, verifying test passage first. Supports both git and Jujutsu (jj) repositories.

plugins.name: handlename-create-pr
plugins.description: Create a Pull Request from the current branch to a base branch, using GitHub CLI to generate a suitable title and description from the commit history.

plugins.name: handlename-draw-mermaid
plugins.description: Draw a mermaid diagram from a natural-language intent and return a syntax-validated mermaid source, checked with mermaid.parse() against a vendored, version-pinned mermaid.js via playwright-cli. Designed to be called from other skills through a subagent.

plugins.name: handlename-github-attachment-upload
plugins.description: Attach a local file to an existing GitHub issue/PR via the GitHub CLI (gh --attach, gh 2.99.0+), returning the user-attachments URL and embed location. File-type agnostic; the target issue/PR is supplied by the caller (comment or body-edit mode), and no throwaway issue is created. Designed to be called from other skills through a subagent.

plugins.name: handlename-github-resource-access
plugins.description: Rules for accessing GitHub resources with the gh CLI: reads are free, writes require an explicit instruction.

plugins.name: handlename-go1.27-changes
plugins.description: Reference for Go 1.27's developer-facing changes (language, standard library, go command) with gotchas foregrounded, for writing or reviewing Go code without falling back on pre-1.27 training-data assumptions.

plugins.name: handlename-hwwwn
plugins.description: Passive reference for what information belongs where and how to phrase code comments: HWWWN routes How to code, What to test code, Why to the commit log, and Why not to code comments (after t_wada), then gives concrete comment rules — minimal, line breaks only at sentence boundaries, and no comment that restates what the code shows. Language/project conventions take precedence.

plugins.name: handlename-maint-glossary
plugins.description: Create and maintain a glossary of domain terms from a requirements document, spec, or codebase — extracting, categorizing, and defining terms for a fresh glossary, and diffing the source to add/revise/deprecate entries when maintaining an existing one.

plugins.name: handlename-mermaid-to-svg
plugins.description: Turn a mermaid diagram into a hand-drawn free-layout SVG image file and return its path. Pure and offline (no mermaid-cli, no browser, no upload). Designed to be called from other skills through a subagent, then paired with github-attachment-upload.

plugins.name: handlename-multirepo
plugins.description: Investigate or edit multiple already-cloned local git repositories in parallel via one multirepo-worker sub-agent per repo. The main session only orchestrates; worktrees are created for edits, and commits/PRs are left to other skills.

plugins.name: handlename-persona-mimic-trainer
plugins.description: Train and iteratively refine a custom sub-agent that mimics a specific person's decision-making criteria, cognitive biases, and communication style for mock wall-hitting (pre-communication verification).

plugins.name: handlename-plan-to-issue
plugins.description: Turn a finalized implementation plan or design into a GitHub tracking issue (overview + PR-granularity checklist plus a self-contained plan issue artifact), or post it as a plan artifact on an existing related issue.

plugins.name: handlename-runbook-execution-support
plugins.description: Support a human operator through a runbook in a GitHub issue comment: step presentation, pre-checks, verification, Slack progress posts, and checklist updates.

plugins.name: handlename-session-supervisor
plugins.description: Run a supervisor session in a Herdr terminal that starts (hc run), tracks, and verifies worker sessions (git worktree, or one per non-git directory), keeps a verified worker for follow-ups until the user confirms its task complete or cancels it and then archives it, keeps a compaction-proof state.json, delegates edits and pushes to workers and observation to subagents, and keeps one Obsidian note per task, where the user answers workers' questions, with a kanban dashboard note.

plugins.name: handlename-setup-tagpr
plugins.description: Set up tagpr for automated release management: creates and updates release pull requests for unreleased items, tags them on merge, and creates GitHub Releases. Supports goreleaser (Go) and TypeScript/Node.js projects.
